alignments.note: The genitive-absolute participle is nominalized as 'in the hearing'; the supplied preposition and determiner are rule 7 helpers, headed on the nominal word.
παντός → all. The quantifier keeps only its own English word; the case preposition belongs to the article under rule 21, not to the word it happens to stand next to.

Rule 21: the genitive article takes 'of the', discontinuous around the preposed quantifier under rule 15. Corrected from a reading that left the article a bare 'the' and gave 'of' to πάντος; the chapter puts 'of the' on the genitive article at 20:10, 20:13, 20:15, 20:20, 20:26, 20:27, 20:36 and 20:39, and rule 57's principle is that an interposed word does not move the article's own English.
Rule 20: the genitive pronoun αὐτοῦ takes the determiner slot.
Dative with its case preposition, discontinuous around the possessive (rules 15, 21).

review_notes: Corrected: 'of' (t005) moves from πάντος to τοῦ, which now carries the discontinuous 'of … the' headed on 'the'.

This makes all nine genitive articles in the chapter uniform under rule 21; the article's determiner is what anchors the case preposition, and rule 21's determinerless clause does not apply because the ASV writes 'the' here.
The dative article τοῖς is untouched and stays unrepresented under rule 20, so the BSB disagreement reported for this verse is unaffected.
